messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: 2 critical symptoms detected in prod-us-west-2
- metric: http5xx_rate /v1/generate > 12% (5m)
- ALB target group tg-llm-prod: 68% unhealthy targets
- proxy logs show repeated TLS handshake failures (ERR_SSL_HANDSHAKE) from edge-ssl-proxy-1
- DNS: observed inconsistent A records in external resolvers (TTL mismatch, some caches returning old IP)
Impact: user-facing 5xxs and elevated tail latency for streaming responses. Potential partial regional outage.
Link: https://pagerduty.example/INC123456 (automated)

eve (oncall): acked. standing up in the thread. tagging owners: @raj @lina @mike. what's the first containment?

pagerduty: Incident INC123456 acknowledged by eve (oncall) at 2026-03-15T02:00:45Z. Next escalation in 5m if not resolved.

raj (sre): seeing the same in grafana. spike started ~02:00 UTC. health checks failing with 502/504. guessing backend pool overload + TLS handshakes failing on edge -> dropped upstream connections. can we pull target health and recent GC/oom logs?

lina (networking): I can check ALB and edge proxies. preliminary: ALB reports many unhealthy because TLS handshake timeout on backend connection attempts. also noticing a surge in SYN_RECV on the edge proxy instances. could be upstream conn stall or a bad cert rotation.

mike (eng-infra): listing target instances now:
```
aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-west-2:123456:targetgroup/tg-llm-prod/abcd1234 --output table
```
Most targets show unhealthy due to `ReceiveTimeout` and `TLS_Handshake_Error`. Last deployment? None in last 6h. No recent cert rotation recorded in infra logs.

carla (support): customers reporting delayed/eager failures for streaming: "tokens stopped mid-stream and then 500". CS queue rising. I'll start an external status note draft once we have containment.

raj (sre): let's do a quick mitigation plan:
1) Fail traffic away from unhealthy AZ/pool by shifting weights (route 60% -> us-east-1 fallback model pool)
2) Bump target healthcheck timeout and re-register targets if flapping
3) Rotate edge proxy TLS session cache (soft restart) on a small set to test
4) If DNS inconsistent, kick off TTL flush and liaise with CDN partner
I'll do 1) now with CLI.

mike (eng-infra): share the command for weight shift when ready. will monitor rollout.

raj (sre): running weight shift CLI:
```
redwoodctl route adjust --route /v1/generate --region us-west-2 --weight 40 && 
redwoodctl route adjust --route /v1/generate --region us-east-1 --weight 60 --reason "emergency failover: tg-llm-prod unhealthy"
```

incident-bot: Automation: route adjust requested by raj. Task queued. Waiting for confirmation from routing service.

pagerduty: PagerDuty: escalated to L2 (raj) and L2 acknowledged. Notification sent to oncall-l2.

lina (networking): while the weight shift is applying, I'm tailing edge logs. snippet:
```
[edge-ssl-proxy-1] 2026-03-15T02:01:12Z TLS handshake error: unsupported protocol at tls_accept
[edge-ssl-proxy-2] 2026-03-15T02:01:18Z ConnPool: upstream conn timeout (500ms)
```
I also see some client IPs hitting old IPs from external resolver caches. that matches DNS TTL skew. coordinating w/ CDN ops to flush.

mike (eng-infra): routing service reports roll started. 60% -> us-east-1 applied in 30s. Monitoring for 5xx rate drop.

eve (oncall): good. raj, can you also try re-registering a couple of healthy targets in us-west to see if they come back green? if it's cert related, re-registering won't help but will show flapping pattern.

raj (sre): re-registering two targets now (i-0a1b2c3d4e, i-0f1e2d3c4b).
```
aws elbv2 register-targets --target-group-arn <arn> --targets Id=i-0a1b2c3d4e Id=i-0f1e2d3c4b
```
They move to healthy -> initial success on i-0a1b2c3d4e but i-0f1e2d3c4b flips back unhealthy after TLS handshake error. looks like a subset of instances have expired JVM TLS caches or older OpenSSL? capturing stack traces.

carla (support): drafting status update: "Partial degradation in US-West for API /v1/generate. We have routed traffic to a fallback region. Engineering is investigating TLS handshake and load balancing. No data loss reported. Next update in 30 minutes or when we have containment." Want me to post?

eve (oncall): post it as a preliminary advisory, mention it's a partial regional issue and we've shifted traffic. tag customers with SLA seats. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: PagerDuty: incident updated - annotation: traffic shifted -> us-east-1 (60%).

lina (networking): CDN ops confirmed TTL anomalies. they purged edge caches for the affected prefix and are republishing correct A records. should stabilize DNS within 90s for cooperating resolvers. I also rolled a soft restart of edge-ssl-proxy-1 (1/3). watching for error rate change.

mike (eng-infra): metrics: http5xx_rate dropped from 12% to 3% in 2 minutes after weight shift. p95 latency for /v1/generate back to baseline for majority of requests. some residual failures where traffic still hits unhealthy targets.

raj (sre): digging into the TLS handshake failure root cause: we see handshake failures specifically when an upstream JVM process tries to reuse a cached TLS session with an old cipher list. suspect an OpenJDK update mismatch across instances. investigating rollout history. if confirmed we'll roll a targeted restart of JVM on bad hosts.

eve (oncall): agree. raj, coordinate the JVM soft restart on the flapping hosts only. lina, keep DNS/CDN flushes going. carla, publish the status update now.

carla (support): posted update to status page and sent emails to impacted customers on SLA list. copied the mitigation steps.

pagerduty: PagerDuty: note added - "Traffic shift applied; investigating TLS session mismatch. L2 engaged."

raj (sre): performing JVM soft restart on i-0f1e2d3c4b (graceful: `systemctl restart redwood-llm --graceful`). will watch healthcheck rejoin.

mike (eng-infra): healthcheck re-evaluated: i-0f1e2d3c4b -> healthy after restart. TLS handshake errors reduced dramatically. rolling restarts queued for 3 other flapping hosts.

lina (networking): CDN reports propagation stabilized, external A records consistent. TTL purge success.

eve (oncall): updating incident severity to Sev2 (partial regional degradation) for tracking. will keep thread open for postmortem. please add root-cause tags and escalation notes.

carla (support): CS notes: customers receiving follow-up with timeline and workaround (traffic routed to fallback region). no lost data, some timeouts recovered.

raj (sre): next steps for RCA: collect JVM versions, recent package updates, cert rotation logs, and deployment windows. I'll start an RCA doc and attach timeline.

eve (oncall): thanks all. summary for Incident channel: initial PagerDuty page for US-West TLS/ALB health, traffic shifted to us-east, TTL/cdn purge coordinated, targeted JVM restart fixed flapping hosts, 5xx rate back to acceptable levels. keeping open for postmortem.

incident-bot: Incident INC123456 transitioned to "stabilized" at 2026-03-15T02:12:00Z. Close when postmortem created.

carla (support): I'll schedule a customer follow-up in 3 hours and add notes to the RCA when it's ready.

mike (eng-infra): logging commands and outputs to incident runbook. tagging runbook: /runbooks/incidents/lb-tls-dns-thundering

pagerduty: PagerDuty: incident INC123456 resolved (stabilized) by eve (oncall) at 2026-03-15T02:13:40Z. Follow-up: RCA assigned to raj.

eve (oncall): assigning RCA to raj, ETA 72h. thanks everyone. end of thread for now. :white_check_mark:
